name: sol_ec_9
description: Unbounded external call return data causing gas griefing/DoS (return bomb)
question: The source file in `source` makes an external call to an untrusted or arbitrary-address contract and then copies, decodes, or otherwise processes the full returned data without limiting or checking the size of returndata first, allowing a malicious callee to return a huge payload that exhausts gas or causes the caller to run out of gas/revert, and this does not apply to calls to fixed, trusted, or protocol-controlled contracts, nor to calls that already bound gas and validate returndatasize before copying.
criteria: Performs a low-level call/staticcall/delegatecall to a user- or externally-supplied address and then copies the entire returndata into memory (e.g. via assembly returndatacopy or by assigning the raw bytes result) without any length check
Calls abi.decode directly on the raw return bytes of an external call to an arbitrary/untrusted address, feeding attacker-controlled oversized data straight into the decoder
Forwards or relays return data from an external call to another contract or event without capping its length, enabling a callee to return an arbitrarily large payload
Iterates over or ABI-decodes an array/struct returned from an untrusted external call without bounding the number of elements processed, allowing gas exhaustion from an oversized response
